uncited: - **Input:** Live voxel textures (e.g., `ImageTexture3D`), model bounding box, camera head position (midpoint between eyes), light direction.
- **Voxel Textures:** 3D textures storing voxel material IDs.
Rasterize a quad mesh sized to the model's orthographic footprint plus a margin for the outline.
The quad is centered on the model's bounding box center.
Convert fragment position to voxel units.
If the march results in a miss, test the four cardinal neighbor pixels.
If any neighbor hit results in `material > 0u`, set `ALBEDO` to `vec3(0.0)` (black outline).
- **Time Complexity:** O(1) per fragment for the quad rasterization and snapping.
Ray marching complexity depends on the voxel density and `march_box` implementation, typically O(N) where N is the number of voxels traversed.
Outline detection adds up to 4 additional ray marches per miss.
Requires storage for voxel textures and bounding box data.
Performance scales with `sigma` (higher sigma means more fragments, but coarser voxel traversal per fragment if optimized) and voxel density.
Outline detection can be expensive if many misses occur.
Not suitable for high-fidelity final rendering.
- **When to use:** VR previews, low-poly voxel art, performance-critical applications where visual fidelity is secondary to consistency.
- **When not to use:** High-resolution rendering, perspective-correct detailed views, scenes with complex lighting requirements beyond simple diffuse.
